## Flutter depth — 3/10

*Gate to leave this phase:* A demo app — navigation, tokens, async, forms and keyed lists — written without dropping into Dart for anything routine.

| | Item | Size | Acceptance |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ✔ | ~~Design tokens~~ | `L` | A `theme` block declares colours, spaces and radii; `padding=md` resolves at compile time; a token in the wrong slot is PUI2304; Flutter emits `AppTokens`/`AppTheme`, HTML emits `--pui-*`. |
| ✔ | ~~`task` — async values~~ | `L` | `task items: List<Todo> = load()` exposes loading/error/value/retry; the generated loader resets before the await and checks `mounted` after it; `examples/async` is widget-tested in CI. |
| ✔ | ~~List identity~~ | `S` | `for item in items key=item.id:` wraps the row in `KeyedSubtree(key: ValueKey(...))`; the key is checked in the loop scope; the todo example uses it. |
| ▸ | **Navigation** | `L` | `screen Detail(id: String)` takes parameters; `navigate Detail(id=x)` and `back()` are checked against the target screen; a project-level route table is generated; an example taps through and back in a widget test. |
| · | Latest-wins task cancellation | `S` | A retry during an in-flight load cannot be overwritten by the older result; a test with two differing delays proves the second result wins. |
| · | Forms and validation | `L` | Typed validators (required, min, max, pattern, email) on `input`; a `form` scope gates `submit`; an invalid submission is impossible to express, not merely discouraged. |
| · | Typed interop | `M` | Host components and imports are declared with signatures, and calls to them are type-checked rather than passed through. |
| · | `derived` values | `M` | `derived total = count * 2` recomputes when its inputs change and never stores state; a widget test shows the derived value updating while an unrelated state change leaves it alone. |
| · | `effect on <state>` | `M` | An effect runs after a change to the states it names and not otherwise; the lowering is `didUpdateWidget` with the same key comparison `useEffect` and `LaunchedEffect` will use. |
| · | Phase gate: the demo app | `M` | One app uses navigation, tokens, async, forms and keyed lists with no hand-written Dart beyond `main.dart`, and is verified in CI like the other examples. |

## v2.0 architecture — 0/4

*Gate to leave this phase:* One `.pui` project compiles to Flutter and Jetpack Compose, both verified in CI, with a test that asserts which files port and which fail with a named code.

| | Item | Size | Acceptance |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| · | The `Target` contract | `L` | Flutter and HTML knowledge (keywords, type names, enum maps, icon names, capabilities) lives behind one interface per target; the front end no longer names a framework. |
| · | Capability matrix and its test | `M` | Every example is compiled for every target; the test asserts which files port and which fail with a code that names the alternative. |
| · | PlainUI type system | `XL` | `Text`/`Int`/`Float`/`Bool`/`Optional` replace Dart spellings in `.pui`, each target maps them, and `plainui migrate` rewrites existing projects. |
| · | Jetpack Compose target | `XL` | A `.pui` project generates Kotlin that compiles under Gradle in CI; `state`, `derived` and `task` lower to `remember`, `derivedStateOf` and `produceState` without special cases. |

## Adoption surface — 1/3

*Gate to leave this phase:* A stranger can install the compiler, add it to an existing app and be productive in ten minutes.

| | Item | Size | Acceptance |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ✔ | ~~`plainui next` — the roadmap as a command~~ | `S` | The roadmap is data in `src/tooling/todo.ts`; `plainui next [--json] [--all] [--phase]` prints it; `docs/11-todo.md` is generated from it and checked by `npm run docs:check`. |
| · | Add PlainUI to an existing Flutter app | `S` | A ten-minute tutorial: install, one screen compiled next to hand-written widgets, one import, no project-wide rewrite. |
| · | Release pipeline | `M` | Version lives in one place; CI packs the tarball, installs it into a scratch project and runs the smoke test before anything is published. |

## Why these, in this order

The phase gate in `docs/09-vision.md` is what decides the order, not preference: the language model
(`state`, `derived`, `effect`, `task`) has to be settled, and one target has to be genuinely deep,
before a second target can be judged a faithful lowering rather than a translation table.
